The bottom arrow points from Jia to Yi and is marked ①; the left arrow points upward from Yi to Bing and is marked ②; the top arrow points from Bing to Ding and is marked ③; the right arrow points downward from Ding to Jia and is marked ④. Then reason: the stem states that the figure represents the sea-land water cycle, and Jia and Yi are underlying surfaces. According to the direction of the arrows in the figure, ① is near-surface horizontal flow from Jia to Yi, which can correspond to terrestrial runoff gathering toward the ocean, namely the runoff link. The formation of the landform of the Loess Plateau is closely related to fluvial erosion and transportation, and the formation of the Yellow River Delta is closely related to the depositional action after the river carries sediment; all of these depend on the river runoff process. Therefore, both are closely related to link ①.
